stories.title: CISA: Hackers now exploit max severity GitLab flaw in attacks
stories.abstract: GitLab has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-85706, a critical path traversal vulnerability carrying a maximum CVSS score of 10.0. CISA has officially added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, signaling widespread risk to unpatched instances.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass security controls and potentially achieve remote code execution, posing a severe risk to infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Update GitLab instances to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include five flaws affecting JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS. These vulnerabilities are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active attacks, necessitating immediate attention from security teams.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or privilege escalation within critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Update JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Revolut handed customer data to fraudsters using government email account
stories.abstract: Revolut inadvertently exposed sensitive customer information after processing fraudulent emergency data requests. Attackers successfully impersonated government officials by utilizing a compromised or spoofed legitimate government email domain to bypass standard verification protocols.
stories.why: This highlights a critical failure in validating emergency data requests, demonstrating how attackers exploit trusted communication channels to bypass security controls.

stories.title: GitLab CVSS 10 File-Read Flaw Draws In-the-Wild Probes After Disclosure
stories.abstract: GitLab has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability, CVE-2026-85706, affecting versions prior to 19.1.8, 19.2.6, and 19.3.2. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server and is currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: The vulnerability carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and is actively exploited, posing an immediate risk of unauthorized data exposure.
stories.action: Update GitLab instances to versions 19.1.8, 19.2.6, or 19.3.2 immediately.

stories.title: Perfect-10 GitLab bug under attack days after patch lands
stories.abstract: GitLab has confirmed active exploitation of a critical vulnerability in its software. Security researchers have observed threat actors scanning the internet to identify and compromise unpatched, publicly accessible instances shortly after the vendor released a security update.
stories.why: The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution, posing a severe risk of full system compromise for exposed GitLab environments.
stories.action: Update GitLab instances to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Cisco FMC Flaws Exploited to Steal Credentials and Deploy Qilin Ransomware
ConnectWise security advisory (AV26-903) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities are actively exploited in ConnectWise ScreenConnect and MikroTik RouterOS. CISA has added several of these flaws, including CVE-2026-84869, CVE-2026-67277, and CVE-2026-86060, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, necessitating immediate patching of affected infrastructure.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are currently being leveraged in real-world attacks, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update ScreenConnect to 26.6.5 and patch MikroTik RouterOS to the latest supported versions immediately.

stories.title: Revolut discloses data breach exposing financial info, passports
Artifactory flaws chained in attacks deploying backdoor malware
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting multiple vulnerabilities in self-hosted JFrog Artifactory instances. These flaws allow unauthorized parties to bypass authentication mechanisms and escalate privileges to administrator, enabling the deployment of malicious Rust-based backdoors on affected servers.
stories.why: Compromised build infrastructure allows attackers to inject malicious code into software supply chains, potentially affecting all downstream users of the build artifacts.
stories.action: Audit JFrog Artifactory logs for unauthorized administrative activity and apply the latest security patches immediately.

stories.title: Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE to Compromise 13 Organizations Across Six Countries
stories.abstract: The threat actor Red Heron is actively targeting internet-facing Gitea instances to achieve remote code execution. The group has scanned over 1,300 servers globally, with a specific focus on organizations located in Taiwan, to facilitate unauthorized system access.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates rapid weaponization of Gitea vulnerabilities, posing a significant risk to organizations hosting internal code repositories and development infrastructure.
stories.action: Audit Gitea instances for unauthorized access and ensure all software versions are fully patched.

stories.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor
stories.abstract: A China-aligned threat actor is exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Sogou Input Method for Windows to distribute the GrayRabbit backdoor. Attackers leverage malicious links to trigger the flaw, granting them full execution privileges under the context of the logged-in user.
stories.why: This represents a supply chain compromise of a widely used utility, providing attackers with persistent, high-privilege access to compromised Windows environments.
stories.action: Update Sogou Input Method to the latest available version immediately.

stories.title: Android security advisory – September 2026 monthly rollup (AV26-920)
stories.abstract: Google has released its September 2026 security bulletin for Android, detailing patches for various vulnerabilities discovered within the mobile operating system. Users and administrators are advised to review the official documentation to determine the impact on their specific device configurations.
stories.why: Timely application of Android security patches is critical to mitigating risks from known exploits that could compromise device integrity and user data.
stories.action: Check for and install the September 2026 Android security update on all managed devices.

stories.title: MongoDB security advisory (AV26-918)
stories.abstract: MongoDB has released security patches for multiple server versions to address a vulnerability involving the improper handling of collection validator constants during the parsing process.
stories.why: Unpatched database servers are primary targets for exploitation, potentially leading to unauthorized data access or service disruption.
stories.action: Update MongoDB Server to version 7.0.43, 8.0.32, 8.3.11, or 9.0.1 as appropriate.

stories.title: Samsung mobile security advisory (AV26-919)
stories.abstract: Samsung has released its September 2026 security maintenance update for mobile devices. This patch addresses several vulnerabilities affecting software versions released prior to the SMR-SEP-2026 designation. Users should verify their device status and apply the latest firmware to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: Unpatched mobile devices are frequent targets for exploitation; applying vendor-supplied security updates is critical to maintaining device integrity and data protection.
stories.action: Update Samsung mobile devices to the SMR-SEP-2026 security release.

stories.title: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data
stories.abstract: Threat actors are leveraging social engineering tactics centered on passkeys and single sign-on prompts to compromise corporate Microsoft 365 accounts. These campaigns, linked to multiple extortion groups, facilitate unauthorized access to cloud environments and subsequent data exfiltration.
stories.why: Attackers are bypassing traditional authentication flows by tricking users into approving fraudulent passkey requests, undermining MFA security postures.
stories.action: Implement FIDO2-compliant hardware security keys and enforce strict conditional access policies for authentication.

stories.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
stories.abstract: The Manhattan District Attorney has seized 12 websites hosting non-consensual, hyper-realistic deepfake sexual imagery. The operation targeted platforms that exploited the likenesses of approximately 1,200 individuals, marking a significant legal escalation against the proliferation of AI-generated non-consensual intimate content.
stories.why: This signals a shift toward aggressive legal intervention against platforms facilitating AI-driven harassment and identity abuse.

stories.title: Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Leaks OAuth Tokens From Nearly 31,000 Users
stories.abstract: A malicious browser extension titled Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot has been caught exfiltrating OAuth tokens from over 31,000 users. The extension transmitted sensitive authentication data to a Russian-based bot service, compromising account security for those who installed the add-on.
stories.why: Stolen OAuth tokens allow attackers to hijack active user sessions, bypass multi-factor authentication, and gain unauthorized access to private account data.
stories.action: Remove the Twitch Enhanced Viewer extension immediately and revoke all active Twitch OAuth tokens.

stories.title: Check Point security advisory (AV26-902)
stories.abstract: The Dutch NCSC warns that active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities in Check Point VPN products is expected soon. The flaws, involving authentication bypass, remote code execution, and heap overflows, impact Security Gateways, Management Servers, and Spark Firewalls.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to gain remote code execution, posing a severe risk to perimeter security and internal network integrity.
stories.action: Apply available security patches for Check Point VPN products immediately.

stories.title: Pro-Ukraine Hacking Cat group deploying new malware against Russian targets
Cyberattack sends International Meteor Organization crashing back to Earth
stories.abstract: The International Meteor Organization suffered a severe cyberattack that crippled its digital infrastructure. The breach caused significant operational downtime, with administrators anticipating several weeks of recovery before systems are fully restored.
stories.why: The incident highlights the vulnerability of specialized research organizations relying on legacy systems to targeted disruptive attacks.

stories.title: OpenAI's malicious bot swarm attacked RubyGems
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a coordinated campaign where automated agents, reportedly leveraging OpenAI technology, flooded the RubyGems repository with hundreds of malicious software packages. The incident highlights the growing risk of AI-driven automation being used to scale supply chain attacks.
stories.why: Automated generation of malicious packages significantly lowers the barrier for attackers to conduct large-scale software supply chain poisoning campaigns.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, September 14th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10092, (Mon, Sep 14th)
stories.abstract: The provided source material for the SANS ISC Stormcast dated September 14, 2026, contains no descriptive content or summary of the day's security events, making it impossible to report on specific incidents or technical developments.

stories.title: Webinar: How malicious OAuth apps can lead to Google Workspace breaches
stories.abstract: Threat actors are increasingly leveraging malicious OAuth applications to bypass traditional credential-based security. By tricking users into granting excessive permissions, attackers gain persistent, unauthorized access to sensitive Google Workspace environments, effectively circumventing standard password protections and multi-factor authentication.
stories.why: OAuth-based attacks represent a significant shift toward identity-centric exploitation, allowing adversaries to maintain access even after password resets.
stories.action: Audit and revoke unnecessary third-party OAuth application permissions within your Google Workspace admin console.

stories.title: SpiderSilk Hunts External Threats With AI-Based Scanner
stories.abstract: Dubai-based startup SpiderSilk has launched an AI-driven platform designed to monitor global IP space. The tool continuously scans for exposed infrastructure, sensitive data leaks, and potential zero-day vulnerabilities to help organizations identify their external attack surface.
stories.why: Automated external attack surface management tools help security teams identify shadow IT and misconfigurations before adversaries can exploit them.

stories.title: New DDRop Attack Breaks Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP Confidential Computing
stories.abstract: Researchers identified DDRop, a hardware-based attack targeting Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP environments. By physically inserting a circuit to suppress memory writes, attackers force processors to process stale, encrypted data, effectively bypassing existing memory isolation protections in confidential computing architectures.
stories.why: This attack undermines the fundamental security guarantees of confidential computing, allowing for data manipulation despite hardware-level encryption and isolation.

stories.title: Hackers target exposed Vite dev servers to steal AWS, Azure secrets
⚡ Weekly Recap: Rogue AI Agents, WeChat Worm, PaperCut Attacks, AI Espionage, and Rootkits
stories.abstract: Recent security trends highlight a dual threat: attackers are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence to automate exploit development and bypass defenses, while simultaneously exploiting persistent vulnerabilities in legacy systems, misconfigured infrastructure, and weak default settings.
stories.why: The integration of AI into offensive toolkits lowers the barrier for sophisticated attacks, while unpatched legacy systems remain primary entry points for adversaries.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-904)
stories.abstract: Google has released a security update for Chrome to address CVE-2026-87491, a vulnerability currently being exploited in the wild. CISA has officially added this flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, signaling a high risk of active exploitation.
stories.why: Active exploitation of browser vulnerabilities poses a direct risk of remote code execution or system compromise for end users.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 153.0.8010.37 or later.

stories.title: UK.gov begins killing off passwords for 23 million users
stories.abstract: The UK government is transitioning 23 million users to passkeys for its One Login service. This initiative aims to replace traditional password authentication with FIDO-based standards, reducing vulnerability to phishing attacks while simultaneously cutting costs associated with SMS-based multi-factor authentication.
stories.why: Widespread adoption of passkeys significantly reduces the risk of credential harvesting and account takeover attacks compared to legacy password and SMS-based authentication methods.

stories.title: ClickFix attacks are tricking Mac and Windows users into hacking themselves
AI Changed the Exposure Problem. Validation Needs to Change With It.
Inside ‘Project Lily’: The Humans Reading Your ChatGPT Chats
stories.abstract: Leaked internal documents reveal that OpenAI employs human reviewers to analyze user prompts from ChatGPT. These transcripts often contain sensitive personal data, which is then utilized to refine the company's underlying artificial intelligence models.
stories.why: Users may inadvertently expose proprietary data, PII, or credentials to human reviewers, violating privacy expectations and potentially leaking sensitive corporate information.
stories.action: Avoid inputting sensitive, confidential, or personal information into public AI chatbots.

stories.title: Chinese Hackers Exploit Critical Tencent Software Flaw for One-Click Code Execution
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in the Tencent Chinese-language input method editor for Windows is being actively exploited by threat actors. The flaw enables remote attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution on target systems through a single-click interaction.
stories.why: Input method editors often run with elevated privileges, making them high-value targets for initial access and persistent system compromise.
stories.action: Disable or remove the Tencent input method editor from Windows systems until a patch is available.

stories.title: Hundreds of fake government websites target users in Central Asia
stories.abstract: A widespread campaign involving hundreds of fraudulent websites is targeting individuals across Central Asia. These portals impersonate government services to harvest contact information, which attackers subsequently leverage for phishing, financial fraud, and unauthorized device access.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates a large-scale social engineering effort designed to compromise personal data and facilitate further exploitation of regional users.
